extracted.intended_audience: federal information managers, librarians, and scientific & technical information (STI) program implementors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for implementing OMB Circular A-130 requirements for scientific and technical information (STI): information dissemination, records management, system acquisition, Web standards, performance measurement, and oversight across federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility for diverse users
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide access to electronic agricultural information to a range of users regardless of whether they have Internet access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alternate access channels (e.g., ALF BBS) and outreach to reach users without standard Internet connectivity; equip services to serve both online and offline communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple dissemination channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Take advantage of all possible dissemination channels (telnet, ftp, gopher, gopher servers, World Wide Web, electronic mail, electronic mailing lists, bulletin boards, dial-in, Mosaic/Lynx/WAIS clients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer content via several methods (anonymous ftp, gopher, Web home pages, mailing lists, bulletin boards) so users can access information using varied clients and network capabilities; examples include NLM, NSF STIS, NOAA, NASA services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic document delivery and interlibrary services
rubrics_metrics.description: Support interlibrary borrowing services and electronic document delivery in addition to mail and fax document delivery operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement online ordering from private-sector document delivery services when expeditious delivery is essential; use scanned page images transmitted via the Internet and maintain international delivery capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation via archival masters
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain archival masters (e.g., silver master microfiche) as official archival records and disaster backups to preserve document integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create archival masters from EDMS raster images; use them to produce duplicates for distribution and as disaster recovery backups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to bibliographic and interchange standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use national and international standards to facilitate access to electronic information (bibliographic cataloging standards and standards for information interchange).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in developing unified thesauri (e.g., Unified Agricultural Thesaurus) and adopt interoperable metadata/format standards to improve worldwide access and reconcilation among existing vocabularies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for subject-specialized information centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish specialized information centers staffed with subject-area experts to provide in-depth coverage and outreach for specific topical areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized centers should produce focused publications, perform outreach to diverse user groups, provide training, and run customer surveys to ensure services meet user needs (examples: NAL's 11 centers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding improperly restrictive dissemination practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Make information services and products as widely available as possible with minimally restrictive practices while preserving integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage multiple dissemination channels; license data to vendors as appropriate but use license agreements to ensure leased data remain accurate, complete, current, and accessible; prevent degradation of critical information that could harm the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable and targeted public access (outreach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in aggressive outreach and programs to ensure those who need information know where and how to obtain it; provide specialized access (e.g., toll-free numbers, cost-free access to critical databases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include NLM's outreach to ensure health professionals and the public can access medical information and the 1994 policy to provide cost-free access to AIDS-related databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization and lifecycle controls for data files
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize data files as raw, verified, or validated and subject them to versioning and controls as they progress through review and assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design information management systems to produce the pedigree of data showing status and nature of changes; implement version numbering, directories, catalogs, and dictionaries to track every data version and provide controlled access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory review/acceptance/approval before publication/use
rubrics_metrics.description: Verified and validated data files must be reviewed, accepted, and approved before being used in validation or published; publication of results is not allowed until the underlying data files are approved and accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suppliers must review data per contracts; aggregation produces verified files that require approval prior to validation and reporting; data reports may be required to document reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance / QA-QC as records
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat data files that contain measurement and QA/QC data as records subject to control and approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure QA/QC metadata are captured and managed under records controls similar to other official documents; include these in approval workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measurement and benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Set performance standards (response time, percentage of complaints, etc.) based on the most restrictive technically practical performance and benchmark against best-in-business practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect performance data as by-products of operations (counts, times), use benchmarking (e.g., National Performance Review) to set standards, and adjust programs annually based on performance trends and new technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational performance metrics and cost accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate performance data (counts, times), report labor hours and costs, and feed these into a unit cost management system to identify costs associated with each product and service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track time to deliver products, availability and reliability of on-line systems, customer satisfaction (complaints); use metrics internally in senior management meetings and incorporate measures in strategic and business plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web server design, interface, and structure standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a minimum set of rules for the design, interface, and structure of Web-based information services to serve as a quality checklist for Web implementors and introductions for new project managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover both human-interface and technical issues; consult other government/commercial/academic style guides; expect periodic updates due to technical advances; the document should list prominent issues to be considered rather than always give specific answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative development and stakeholder review of standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop standards through iterative drafting and circulation to interested parties, incorporating hands-on implementation experience and ad hoc contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circulate multiple draft versions, use internal communication channels (e.g., e-mail lists) for contributions, and revise the standard as implementors gain experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central management oversight and governance for system reinvention
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a single high-level oversight group to direct and coordinate system reinvention projects, evaluate working group plans, approve milestones, review resource requirements, and coordinate system transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The oversight committee should set priorities across production systems, recommend transition courses of action, and ensure adequate resources for upgrade projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define primary components for system reinvention
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure new systems support mission requirements by organizing work around four primary components: the Access Model, Retrieval Systems, File Generation and Maintenance, and Integrated Library Systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign working groups to concentrate expertise on each area to manage upgrades and transitions from R&D to production systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use off-the-shelf commercial solutions where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt an operating philosophy of favoring off-the-shelf hardware and software ("invent nothing"), modifying commercial products only as necessary to meet government requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark private-sector tools to determine useful publishing and inventory systems; implement scalable commercial platforms (examples: NTIS FedWorld®, NASA modernization using commercial off-the-shelf software).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing, licensing, and statutory compliance (NTIS example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charge licensing and use fees in compliance with statutory requirements and OMB A-130 guidance; apply marginal pricing philosophy across operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize statutory exemptions (e.g., NTIS products exempt from FOIA) and provide services to other agencies to support FOIA compliance when requested; fees may be charged because of self-supporting agency status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata, catalogs, and data directories for provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and implement a data directory, catalog, and dictionary to track and document all versions of data generated or managed and to provide access to external data required by programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The information management system must produce pedigree information demonstrating status and changes (raw→verified→validated) and protect the integrity of file contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: User feedback integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase Internet availability to facilitate user surveys and feedback so customer input can refine offerings and ensure systems meet community information needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect customer feedback via online channels and use it to guide system and service refinements; evaluate usage patterns (e.g., NASA Select usage) to identify products of greatest interest.
